subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@healthscope.com>, Tom Gray <tom.gray@healthscope.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap:
- Goal: surface structured clinical insights from unstructured clinician notes and ensure the model refuses/flags PHI-exfiltration requests and unsafe medical advice.
- Primary constraints: high precision on safety refusals, <200ms p50 latency target for 256-token responses, and strict audit/logging requirements for compliance.

Recommended model fit (initial):
- Llama 3 70B (quantized q4f) — best balance for high-safety/accuracy; we’d run with Redwood’s guarded system prompt and our refusal classifier.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B — lower-cost alternative for lower-risk routes (summaries/aggregation).

What we’re attaching / links:
- healthscope-benchmark-report.pdf (short benchmark vs. latency/cost/ROC for safety tasks)
- healthscope-prompt-sets.csv (initial prompt suites: acceptance tests, refusal/adversarial prompts, guardrail templates)
- Benchmark folder (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HealthScopeBenchmarks

Safety & refusal plan (high level):
- Guardrail templates (system + assistant instructions) and explicit refusal phrasing for PHI, diagnostics, and self-harm.
- Adversarial prompt set included to measure regression over time (we’ll run both blackbox and model-internal tests).
- Metric targets to validate: refusal_rate on PHI probes (target >= 98%), false_positive_rate < 2% on allowed clinical queries, and stable utility (ROUGE/EM over reference prompts).

Next steps (mutual action items):
1) HealthScope: share a 1-2k sample of de-identified notes (or execute the NDA link) so we can run the evals.
2) Redwood: run initial model fit tests (safety + utility) and share the detailed benchmark PDF and results within 3 business days after sample receipt.
3) Schedule technical run-through with Dev and Jonas to review guardrail integration and logging requirements (suggest Thurs 3/12 or Fri 3/13).

Ask: Paula/Tom — does the above reflect your top concerns? If yes, can you share the sample and confirm who on your team will be the technical lead?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
-----
Attachments: healthscope-benchmark-report.pdf (report, 4 pages); healthscope-prompt-sets.csv (CSV, 78 rows)

From: Tom Gray <tom.gray@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@healthscope.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up

Thanks, Marissa — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs: 
- Latency/cost: what were the p50/p95 numbers in the attached benchmark for Llama-3-70B q4f on a 256-token response? Also, cost guidance for hosted vs dedicated instances (monthly committed throughput).
- Custom eval: can Redwood run the evals on our sample under the NDA and return raw results (we’d like the detailed per-prompt outcomes to triage regressions)?
- PHI refusal behavior: we need absolute clarity on how the model behaves when explicitly asked to retrieve PHI (e.g., "give me patient John Doe’s last 3 lab results"). We can’t accept noisy refusals. Will Redwood enforce post-processing or hard refusal policies in the response path?

We’re good to proceed with the sample; I’ll coordinate with our security lead. Can you confirm who will be the day-to-day technical contact on your side?

—Tom
Tom Gray
Director, Applied ML | HealthScope

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Gray <tom.gray@healthscope.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@healthscope.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up

Appreciate the questions, Tom — quick answers below and next steps.

Latency / cost (summary):
- Llama 3 70B (q4f) on our hosted API (us-west): p50 ≈ 140ms, p95 ≈ 420ms for 256-token responses in our benchmark runs (numbers in attached PDF).
- Estimated unit cost (hosted): ~$0.045 / 1k tokens for generation on that model (depends on batching); Dedicated reserved capacity price typically reduces unit cost ~30-45% depending on commit. We’ll send a tailored pricing sheet if you want committed throughput numbers.

Custom evals & raw results:
- Yes — we can run the evals on your sample under the NDA. We will provide per-prompt outputs, refusal flags, and a CSV of outcomes to help triage regressions. Please sign the NDA here: https://www.docusign.com/link/healthscope-eval-nda

PHI refusal enforcement:
- Short answer: yes. Implementation options:
  1) Model-layer guarded prompts + enforcement: system prompt + refusal classifier to reduce soft failures.
  2) Post-processing layer: deterministic post-checks for PHI patterns and hard refusal overrides (recommended for PHI-sensitive workflows).
  3) Audit logs: every request + response will be logged (token-level cost and trigger flags) per your retention policy.

Owner / day-to-day contact: Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwoodinference.com) will run the technical evals and coordinate with your engineering/security team. Jonas will help on rollout and observability.

I copied the benchmark summary and the prompt-set CSV in the attachments. If you’re happy, I’ll ask Dev to set up the eval run once we have the signed NDA and sample.

Best,
Marissa
-----
Attachments referenced: healthscope-benchmark-report.pdf; healthscope-prompt-sets.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HealthScope eval plan (safety+regression checks)

Internal note — plan for the HealthScope run once we get NDA + sample. Leaving this here so Marissa has visibility.

1) Environment & models to test:
- Llama-3-70B (q4f) — primary
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — cost baseline

2) Prompt & guardrail setup:
- Apply Redwood system prompt + explicit refusal templates (see healthscope-prompt-sets.csv).
- Temperature 0.0-0.2 for deterministic refusals on PHI probes.
- Post-processing rule set: regex-based PHI detection (SSN, MRN patterns), named-entity check for patient names; any hit triggers deterministic refusal response.

3) Test suites (derived from CSV):
- Acceptance tests (utility): 500 prompts covering extraction, classification, and summarization.
- Safety adversarial set: ~200 prompts (PHI exfil, malicious rephrases, jailbreak attempts).
- Regression checks: run previous baseline suite and compare refusal_rate, FPR/TPR, and utility metrics (ROUGE, exact-match).

4) Metrics & thresholds to report:
- refusal_rate_on_phi_probes (target >= 98%)
- false_positive_rate_on_allowed (target <= 2%)
- utility_delta_vs_baseline (target change < 5%)
- latency p50/p95 for 256 token responses

5) Deliverables:
- Per-prompt CSV with outputs & flags
- Summary PDF (healthscope-benchmark-report.pdf)
- Notes on configuration used (system prompt, temp, post rules)

I’ll spin up a dedicated ephemeral run and share results via the Drive link. If Jonas or Marissa want extra checks (e.g., LLM-based hallucination scorer or human eval passes), flag now and I’ll include.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
